questions.q: What is the article mainly about?
options: How insurers are raising premiums on beachfront homes across Orange County
How a strong El Niño and warming are bringing flooding and fire to California
How the Santa Ana winds have shaped wildfire policy in Southern California
How a state budget fight is delaying disaster relief for coastal towns
questions.explain: It describes flooding in Dana Point and a fire in San Juan Capistrano tied to El Niño and climate change.

questions.q: How many acres did the Norte fire consume?
questions.explain: The Norte fire consumed 570 acres and burned at least seven houses.

questions.q: How much emergency funding did the Orange County Transportation Authority secure for the coastal tracks?
questions.explain: It secured $308 million in emergency funding to protect the coastal tracks.

questions.q: Why doesn't Lori Torres' insurance cover her damage?
options: Her policy excludes homes built directly on the coastline
The damage was classified as a pre-existing foundation defect
The water has not flooded the interior of the house
She had not renewed the flood rider since buying in 2019
questions.explain: Because the water hasn't flooded the interior, insurance doesn't cover the damage.

questions.q: What does Representative Levin's 'new normal' comment suggest?
options: Such combined threats will keep recurring
questions.explain: He said climate change is not theoretical and Californians face more threats than ever.
